newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse marginally up in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse marginally up in moderate trade.

text.p: The Irish bourse ended marginally up on Friday in moderate trading, with the market reassured by news that U.S. producer prices had fallen by more than expected, easing worries over a near-term hike in U.S. interest rates, dealer said.

"We're off the top on financials but elsewhere quite buoyant," one dealer said. "The market has held up relatively well considering last night's fall and of course we're relieved to see the U.S. figures."
News that U.S. producer prices had fallen 0.4 percent in February, instead of the 0.1 percent fall expected, eased fears and UK gilts and equities ticked higher in response.
On the Irish bourse financials opened easier but were pushing better towards the end of business, dealers said.
"AIB and Bank of Ireland are both down but there's no great volume so there's no great pressure on the stock at present," a dealer said.
Interest in secondline stocks continued to be strong, dealers said, while food company Avonmore had added 15 pence to its share price.
Dealers said that trade volumes could have been better but had been damped down by the approach of the St Patrick's Day holiday weekend, with many brokers leaving their books early.
Among leading financials AIB fell four pence to 445, Bank of Ireland dropped six pence to 642, while Irish Life was down five pence at 325, and Irish Permanent fell three pence to 620.
Among leading industrials, food stock Avonmore gained 15 pence to 250 while CRH fell six pence to 641. Kerry Group was down five pence to 655.
By 1610 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was up 6.07 points or 0.20 percent at 3,048.20.
Elsewhere the FTSE 100 cut its losses, rising to the day's best levels after the Dow opened higher on the weaker-than-expected U.S. price data.
